response.sql: WITH item_town AS (SELECT ili.order_item_id, c.town_city, AVG(ili.product_price) AS avg_price, AVG(ili.derived_product_cost * 1.0 / NULLIF(ili.derived_total_cost, 0)) AS avg_ratio FROM Invoice_Line_Items ili JOIN Invoices i ON i.invoice_number = ili.invoice_number JOIN Orders o ON o.order_id = i.order_id JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY ili.order_item_id, c.town_city), town AS (SELECT town_city, AVG(avg_price) AS avg_price, AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM item_town GROUP BY town_city), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS overall_ratio FROM town) SELECT t.town_city, t.avg_price, t.avg_ratio, t.avg_ratio - o.overall_ratio AS ratio_above_average FROM town t CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE t.avg_ratio > o.overall_ratio ORDER BY ratio_above_average DESC

assumptions.assumption: The 'average across all towns' is the simple mean of the per-town average ratios, so each town counts equally. It is not a mean over all line items.
A line with derived_total_cost of 0 gets a NULL ratio (via NULLIF) and is ignored, like other missing values.
Customers with a NULL town_city form their own group and are kept. Such a group is included in the cross-town average, and it can appear in the result only if its ratio is above average.
